tracks.legalName: Application for Expungement of a Non-Conviction Record, I.C. § 67-3004(10)

controllingAuthority.summary: Expungement reaches only non-conviction records held by the state police. The Idaho State Police Bureau of Criminal Identification publishes a single statewide application and rejects anything incomplete.

eligibleRecordTypes: fingerprint and criminal history record taken in connection with the incident
official court file, which may be sealed
eligibleDispositions: arrested or served a criminal summons and not charged by indictment or information within one year of the arrest or summons
acquitted of all offenses arising from the arrest or summons
exclusions: The form adds that the process does not apply to a person convicted of a sex offense, and directs those users to the Idaho Central Registry sex offender FAQ rather than to the Criminal History Unit.

waitingPeriods.condition: No-charge route: arrested or served a criminal summons and not charged

tracks.legalName: Petition to Shield Records from Public Disclosure, I.C. § 67-3004(11)
tracks.publicName: Shielding a Record from Public Disclosure

citations: I.C. § 67-3004(11), added by 2023 chapter 108, effective January 1, 2024
Idaho Supreme Court, Petition to Shield Records from Public Disclosure, 01/01/2024
controllingAuthority.summary: Shielding hides a court record from the public but does not destroy it. The court shall order shielding if it finds eligibility, that the petitioner has been held accountable, and that shielding would not compromise public safety or the safety of any victims. Paragraph (l) makes the procedures subject to the rules of the Idaho Supreme Court.

eligibleDispositions: arrested for, prosecuted for, or convicted of a misdemeanor that is not on the assaultive or violent list
arrested for, prosecuted for, or convicted of felony possession of a controlled substance under § 37-2732(a), (c), or (e)
exclusions: The thirteen assaultive or violent misdemeanors under § 67-3004(11)(b): assault (§ 18-901); battery (§ 18-903); domestic battery (§ 18-918); stalking in the second degree (§ 18-7906); violation of a protection order or no contact order (§§ 18-7907 and 18-920); telephone harassment (§ 18-6710); vehicular manslaughter (§ 18-4006(3)(c)); excessive driving under the influence (§ 18-8004C); domestic assault (§ 18-918(3)(a)); battery upon law enforcement (§ 18-915(1)(b)); injury to children (§ 18-1501); sexual battery (§ 18-924); and indecent exposure (§ 18-4116).
One petition granted per lifetime, covering one eligible crime, or more than one eligible crime if committed in a single incident or transaction, § 67-3004(11)(k).

waitingPeriods.condition: Completion of the sentence in full, including all ordered probation, parole, fines, and restitution. Unpaid fines or restitution stop the clock from starting.

geography.venue: The county court where the underlying criminal case was filed. The proceeding occurs in the underlying criminal case, § 67-3004(11)(e). E-filing available through iCourt.

destination.name: District court, in the underlying criminal case
destination.detail: File in the county court where the underlying criminal case was filed, or e-file through iCourt. No filing fee. The court notifies the prosecuting attorney of the hearing date; service on the prosecutor is not the petitioner's job.

components.notes: Petition to Shield Records from Public Disclosure, I.C. § 67-3004(11), 01/01/2024. Statewide approved form.

participantInputs.question: Have you ever had a shielding petition granted in Idaho before? Only one is allowed in a lifetime.
What was the exact charge and statute section, and was it a misdemeanor or a felony?
On what date did you finish your sentence, including all probation, parole, fines and restitution?
Have you been convicted of any felony or misdemeanor since then?
Do you have any misdemeanor or felony case pending, are you on probation or parole for a later conviction, or is any restraining order in effect against you?
In your own words, how have you been held accountable, and why would shielding this record not compromise public safety or the safety of any victim?
What is the case number, and which county was the case filed in?

rules.filing: File in the county court where the underlying criminal case was filed, or e-file through iCourt. Complete the petition in black ink or by typing. For paper filing, bring an original plus one copy; the clerk date-stamps the copy.
rules.notice: On the filing of the petition the court shall set a hearing date and notify the prosecuting attorney, who must give any readily identifiable victim the notifications required by article I, section 22 of the Idaho Constitution.

rules.notarization: The source review does not state a notarization requirement for this petition.

selfHelpStopConditions: The prosecutor opposes the Clean Slate petition or a victim appears and objects.
The court signals it will take testimony.
The offense classification against the thirteen-item list or against § 37-2732(a), (c), or (e) is genuinely unclear.
The person has any subsequent charge, conviction, active supervision, or restraining order inside the five-year window or before the hearing.
Restitution or fines remain unpaid, which means the clock has not started.
The person has already used their one lifetime shielding petition, or is choosing between records and needs advice on which to spend it on.
A § 19-2604 dismissal already happened or is being contemplated, because the sequencing changes what relief remains.
The record involves sex offender registration.
A DUI is involved and the § 18-8004 versus § 18-8004C question controls.
The person wants their firearm rights or civil rights back, which is §§ 18-310 and 18-3316 territory and is untouched by shielding.
The record is federal, tribal, or from another state.
Immigration, professional licensing, peace officer employment, or firearm consequences are in play.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: Original review: "Approved with limitations. Three limitations: the one-per-lifetime rule makes track selection consequential and should carry an explicit warning; the DUI question in section 0.3 item 4 needs Lawrence's answer before any DUI user is routed; and the accountability and public-safety showing is the substance of the petition and needs an approved approach rather than a template paragraph." The amendment resolves the operational treatment of the narrative and the hearing; the DUI classification remains a true blocker.

limitations.statement: Shielding has no effect on the operation of §§ 18-310 and 18-3316, the civil rights and firearm provisions. The proceedings are deemed never to have occurred subject to four carve-outs: judicial proceedings; the peace officer licensing process; paragraph (i); and paragraph (j), which gives POST-certified peace officers and prosecuting attorneys complete access.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACK 2 - CLEAN SLATE SHIELDING / Legal effect and limits
provenance.sourceStatement: The proceedings are deemed never to have occurred and the person may lawfully reply accordingly, subject to four carve-outs: judicial proceedings; the peace officer licensing process; paragraph (i), which preserves the operation of §§ 18-310 and 18-3316; and paragraph (j), which gives POST-certified peace officers and prosecuting attorneys complete access for victim communication, in-court purposes, hearings, investigations, and enhancements.

tracks.legalName: Application for Set-Aside, Dismissal and Discharge, I.C. § 19-2604(1)
tracks.publicName: Set aside your conviction and have the case dismissed

controllingAuthority.summary: Where sentence was imposed but suspended, or was withheld, on the defendant's application and a satisfactory showing of compliance with probation, or graduation from an authorized drug court or mental health court program, the court may terminate the sentence or set aside the plea or conviction and finally dismiss the case and discharge the defendant. Final dismissal restores civil rights. It does not hide the record and it is not an expungement.

eligibleDispositions: graduation from an authorized drug court or mental health court program with compliance during any subsequent probation
exclusions: An offense requiring sex offender registration under § 18-8304 is not subject to dismissal or reduction under this section. "Conviction" here includes a plea or finding of guilt notwithstanding the form of the judgment or a withheld judgment.

provenance.sourceStatement: A custom pleading is permissible in principle if counsel confirms the current statutory elements, caption, venue, required attachments, service, proposed-order practice, and any county variation.

provenance.sourceHeading: Idaho operational amendments / True blockers retained
provenance.sourceStatement: Any current § 19-2604 statutory amendments or local form requirements must be source-approved before release.

legalDesignDecision.rationale: The amendment moves this track off "Additional research required" to "custom_pleading, legal-design blocked pending statewide/local filing confirmation", separating the known remedy from the unresolved output specification. The remedy, authority, effect and exclusion are imported; the filing vehicle is preserved as a blocker.

limitations.statement: Accepted statewide versus county-specific filing vehicle and complete pleading requirements remain unresolved. This is a true output-strategy blocker, not a record-review requirement.

provenance.sourceStatement: **ID-3 and ID-4:** accepted statewide versus county-specific filing vehicle and complete pleading requirements remain unresolved. This is a true output-strategy blocker, not a record-review requirement.

limitations.statement: A reduction under § 19-2604(2) does not hide the record and is not an expungement.

provenance.sourceHeading: TRACKS 3 and 4 - SET-ASIDE, DISMISSAL, AND FELONY REDUCTION
provenance.sourceStatement: Effect: final dismissal restores civil rights. It does **not** hide the record, and it is not an expungement.

limitations.statement: An offense requiring sex offender registration under § 18-8304 is not subject to dismissal or reduction under this section.
